first.rationale: Two of the three current symptoms (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) are funnel-friction symptoms, and the inherited record most directly addressed to them is the onboarding/signup-simplification line (memory_31, memory_86). That is also the option most consistent with the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue: it compounds and does not buy volume with margin. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the tempting reflex against the competitor's entry pricing, but discount-led acquisition tends to import exactly the price-sensitive, low-durability accounts the competitor is already courting, and it trades near-term acquisition against long-run qualified revenue; I am deliberately not spending the single slot there. I spend the verification budget on memory_31 and memory_86 rather than on the option I am declining, because those two are the evidence I would actually act on and they are suspiciously parallel: both are archived consolidations that could easily be two summaries of one underlying experiment, in which case my apparent corroboration is a single data point counted twice. I also want the original records to confirm what the lift was measured on. Key downstream risk, flagged: 'simplification' historically means stripping required signup fields, which can lift raw activation while degrading firmographic/qualification signal, routing enterprise-shaped prospects away from the sales-assisted path that memory_44 says converts better, and thereby raising activation counts while lowering qualified revenue. So the experiment must be guarded: keep the demo-request/sales-assist branch intact and prominent, hold out a control, and gate the read on downstream qualified pipeline and retained revenue, not on activation or completion alone. Uncertainty preserved: all six memories are 15-64 days stale and predate the competitor's entry pricing, so their effect sizes may not transfer to the current mix; if the archive shows memory_31 and memory_86 share a source or measured only top-of-funnel proxies, I would downgrade to a small guarded test and treat activation_messaging (memory_91) as the cheaper in-product alternative that does not touch qualification data.

final.rationale:
The archive resolved my main worry: exp_31 and exp_86 are genuinely distinct experiments, not one result double-counted, so the onboarding-friction line has two independent confirmations rather than one. Crucially, both were measured deep enough to be trusted on the dimension I actually care about. exp_31 carried the lift through to qualified revenue (+4%) with only a -1% retention wobble, and exp_86 improved 30-day retention (+3%) alongside a 2.1-day cut in time-to-value. That is the profile of a durable funnel fix rather than a volume trick, and it maps directly onto the two symptoms in front of me (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%). I am spending the single slot here.

I am still declining promotional_pricing (memory_73) despite it being the reflexive answer to the competitor's entry pricing. Discount-led acquisition selects for exactly the price-sensitive, low-durability accounts the competitor is already bidding for, and memory_73 was never verified down to retained/qualified revenue. Trading margin and mix for headline acquisition is the wrong move against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and it would also start a price war I cannot win from one experiment slot.

Guardrails, because the archive also sharpened the risk. exp_31's conclusion is explicit that it holds on SMB and was NOT replicated on other segments, so I scope the treatment to SMB self-serve only and leave the enterprise demo-request/sales-assist path (memory_44) fully intact and prominent. The specific failure mode is that stripping required signup fields lifts activation counts while degrading firmographic/qualification signal and silently diverting enterprise-shaped prospects out of the higher-converting assisted flow, i.e. more activations and less qualified revenue. So: randomized holdout control, treatment limited to SMB self-serve, no removal of fields used for enterprise routing or lead scoring, and the read gated on downstream qualified pipeline and retained revenue rather than on completion or activation alone.

Uncertainty preserved. Both source records are 15-64 days old and predate the competitor's entry pricing, so the SMB mix they were measured on may no longer be the mix I am acquiring; effect sizes should be treated as directional, not as forecasts. exp_86 never measured qualified revenue at all, so the revenue case rests on exp_31's modest +4% alone. I also watch exp_31's -1% retention dip: small and possibly noise, but if it widens under current conditions the compounding argument weakens. If the qualified-revenue read comes back flat or the enterprise routing metrics degrade, I stop, and activation_messaging (memory_91) becomes the fallback next cycle since it lifts week-one engagement without touching qualification data.
